standard.title: Features of an Asian Society in the 18th and Early 19th Century
standard.description: the key social, cultural, economic and political features of an Asian society during the 18th and early 19th Century
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have examined Asia-Pacific societies in Year 8, including features, power structures, and significant events of pre-modern Asian societies. They understand concepts of imperial power, cultural features, and economic organisation from earlier study. This descriptor establishes the baseline understanding of one selected Asian society before examining the effects of European contact (K20–K24).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate the key social, cultural, economic and political features of one Asian society during the 18th and early 19th century.

nodes.label: Political features and structure of the selected society
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the key political features of the selected Asian society including the role of the ruling authority and the structure of governance.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the political structure of the selected Asian society, including who held power and how it was exercised.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate the political features of the selected society: for China — the Qing dynasty, the role and influence of the Emperor, the examination system, and the bureaucratic structure; for India — the territorial extent of the Mughal Empire, the role and influence of the Mughal Emperor, and the relationship between central and regional power; for Japan — the influence of the Tokugawa Shogunate, the role of the Emperor (nominal), the feudal hierarchy of daimyo and samurai, and the policy of sakoku (controlled isolation).
wider: Compare the political structures of two Asian societies at the same period — examining how Qing China's bureaucratic imperial system, Mughal India's hierarchical sultanate, and Tokugawa Japan's feudal structure represented different approaches to governance with different consequences for stability and reform

Examine how political legitimacy was constructed and maintained in the selected society — through religion, ritual, military power, economic redistribution, or cultural production — and assess which mechanisms were most important
nodes.hinge_reason: A clear understanding of the political structure of the selected society before European contact is essential for understanding what changed and what was threatened when contact intensified (K20). Without this baseline, students cannot evaluate the significance of colonial effects.

response_modes.reason: Establishing accurate knowledge of the political structure of the selected society is a foundational step. Students who confuse the Tokugawa Shogunate with the Emperor, or the Mughal court structure with later British Raj administration, will struggle with all subsequent analysis.

success_criteria: Describes the political structure of the selected Asian society, identifying who held formal authority and how governance was organised
Explains at least one feature of how political power was maintained or legitimised

nodes.label: Social, cultural and economic features
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate the significant social, cultural and economic features of the selected Asian society, including cultural production and economic organisation.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two social, cultural or economic features of the selected Asian society.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate the significant features of the selected society: for China — the role of cultural features (art, literature, architecture), the importance of Confucian social hierarchy, and trade networks; for India — the art and architecture of Mughal India (e.g. Taj Mahal), the social structure including the role of religion, and trade connections; for Japan — the role of Buddhism and Shinto, samurai culture, artistic traditions, and the system of controlled trade with China and the Netherlands.
wider: Examine how cultural production (art, architecture, literature) in the selected society expressed and reinforced political and religious authority — analysing specific examples as evidence of the society's values and power structures

Investigate the trade networks of the selected Asian society and its connections with other regions — examining how economic relationships with neighbouring and distant societies shaped the selected society before European pressure intensified
Examine how social hierarchy structured daily life for different groups in the selected society — exploring gender roles, caste or class distinctions, and the experiences of marginalised communities

response_modes.reason: Covering social, cultural, and economic dimensions gives a rounded picture of the selected society — reducing to only political features produces an impoverished understanding of what European contact disrupted.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Asian societies in the 18th and early 19th century were not passive or underdeveloped — they had sophisticated cultural, economic, and political systems. The pedagogical opportunity here is to establish genuine respect for and understanding of these societies as complex historical entities before examining European impact.
success_criteria: Investigates at least three significant features of the selected Asian society across at least two domains (social, cultural, economic)
Describes at least one cultural feature that reveals something about the society's values or power structure
